rules.title: Unexpected shutdown with Kernel-Power
rules.finding: Unexpected shutdown pattern detected. Possible power outage, PSU issue, hardware instability or system crash.
recommendations: Check power supply, UPS and power stability.
Check system temperatures.
Run memory diagnostics.

rules.title: Kernel-Power 41
rules.finding: Kernel-Power Event 41: the system restarted without a clean shutdown.
recommendations: Check power supply and temperatures.

rules.title: Unexpected shutdown 6008
rules.finding: An unexpected shutdown was recorded (Event 6008).
recommendations: Investigate unexpected shutdowns.

rules.title: System crash (bugcheck)
rules.finding: The system crashed with a stop error (blue screen) and restarted.
recommendations: Note the bugcheck code in the event data and look it up.
Update or roll back recently installed drivers and updates.
Analyze the memory dump with WinDbg.

rules.title: Disk errors with NTFS corruption
rules.finding: Disk errors and NTFS corruption detected. Storage subsystem failure is likely.
recommendations: Backup critical data immediately.
Run SMART diagnostics on all disks.
Run CHKDSK /F and review storage logs.

rules.title: Disk bad blocks
rules.finding: Disk bad sectors detected. Check SMART health immediately.
recommendations: Check SMART health immediately.
Schedule disk replacement planning.

rules.title: NTFS corruption
rules.finding: File system corruption detected. Run CHKDSK and verify disk health.
recommendations: Run CHKDSK /F.
Investigate previous unexpected shutdowns.

rules.title: Disk predicts failure
rules.finding: A disk reports that it is about to fail (SMART). Treat it as failing.
recommendations: Back up critical data immediately.
Replace the failing disk as soon as possible.

rules.title: Repeated storage I/O problems
rules.finding: Repeated storage I/O errors, retries or device resets. A disk, cable, controller or driver may be failing.
recommendations: Check SMART health and disk firmware.
Check cables, backplane and the storage controller driver and firmware.
Make sure critical data is backed up.

rules.title: Low disk space
rules.finding: A disk is almost full or shadow copies could not grow.
recommendations: Free space on the affected drive.
Move or archive old data, or extend the volume.

rules.title: Boot or system driver failed to load
rules.finding: A boot-start or system-start driver failed to load.
recommendations: Identify the driver in the event text and reinstall or roll it back.
Run sfc /scannow if system files may be damaged.

rules.title: Repeated service crashes
rules.finding: Services are terminating unexpectedly (3 or more times). Identify the affected service in the event text.
recommendations: Identify the crashing service in the event text.
Check the Application log and the service's own logs.
Review the service's recovery settings.

rules.title: Services failing to start
rules.finding: Several services failed to start or hung while starting.
recommendations: Read the error in each event text.
Check service accounts and dependencies.

rules.title: Domain or Group Policy connectivity problems
rules.finding: The computer has trouble reaching its domain controller (Netlogon or Group Policy errors).
recommendations: Check network connectivity and DNS settings.
Check that a domain controller is reachable.
Check time synchronization and the computer account.

rules.title: Time synchronization problems
rules.finding: The Windows Time service cannot reach a reliable time source.
recommendations: Check the configured time source and network access to it.
Run w32tm /query /status.

rules.title: Fatal hardware error
rules.finding: A fatal hardware error was reported by the hardware (WHEA).
recommendations: Open the event details to see the failing component.
Run vendor hardware diagnostics and update firmware.

rules.title: Repeated corrected hardware errors
rules.finding: Repeated corrected hardware errors (WHEA). The hardware is recovering from errors that may get worse.
recommendations: Open the event details to see the component.
Check cooling and power; update BIOS and device firmware.

rules.title: CPU throttled by firmware
rules.finding: The processor is repeatedly being slowed by firmware (heat or power limits).
recommendations: Check cooling, fans and dust.
Check the power plan and power supply.

rules.title: Display driver resets
rules.finding: The display driver stopped responding and was reset more than once.
recommendations: Update the graphics driver.
Check GPU temperature and power.

rules.title: IP address conflict
rules.finding: An IP address conflict was detected on the network.
recommendations: Find the device with the conflicting address (its MAC address is in the event).
Check DHCP scope and static address assignments.

rules.title: Repeated TLS failures
rules.finding: Repeated TLS (Schannel) connection failures. A client or server may use unsupported TLS settings or certificates.
recommendations: Identify the client that is connecting and its TLS settings.
Review certificates and TLS/cipher settings on the server.

rules.title: Event log cleared
rules.finding: An event log was cleared. Confirm this was an authorized action.
recommendations: Confirm the clearing was authorized and check who did it.

rules.title: New service installed
rules.finding: A new service was installed. Confirm it is expected.
recommendations: Confirm the new service is expected; check its name and file path.

rules.title: DistributedCOM warnings
rules.finding: DistributedCOM warnings detected. Usually low risk and often harmless.
recommendations: DistributedCOM warnings are usually low priority.

rules.title: Many failed logons
rules.finding: Many failed logons in a short time. Possible password guessing or a service with a wrong password.
recommendations: Check the top failed accounts and source addresses in the Security summary.
Block or investigate the source if it is not a known computer.
Check for services or tasks using an old password.

rules.title: Account lockouts
rules.finding: One or more accounts were locked out.
recommendations: Find the computer causing the failed logons (caller computer in the lockout event).
Check for old saved passwords, mapped drives and services.

rules.title: New account added to a group
rules.finding: A new account was created and added to a group within an hour. Confirm this was authorized.
recommendations: Confirm who created the account and added it to the group.
Review the members of privileged groups.

rules.title: Group membership changes
rules.finding: Security group membership was changed.
recommendations: Confirm the changes were authorized, especially for Administrators and other privileged groups.

rules.title: Security log cleared
rules.finding: The Security audit log was cleared. Confirm this was authorized.
recommendations: Check who cleared the log and why.
Review events around this time on other computers.

rules.title: Audit policy changed
rules.finding: The system audit policy was changed.
recommendations: Confirm the change was authorized and check what was changed.

rules.title: New service or scheduled task (audit)
rules.finding: A service or scheduled task was created (audit events). Confirm it is expected.
recommendations: Check the service or task name and the program it runs.

rules.title: Repeated application crashes
rules.finding: Applications are crashing or hanging repeatedly (3 or more times).
recommendations: Note the faulting application and module in the event data.
Update or reinstall the program; check recent updates and drivers.

rules.title: Low virtual memory
rules.finding: Windows ran low on virtual memory.
recommendations: Find the memory-hungry program listed in the event.
Add memory or increase the page file.

rules.title: Volume Shadow Copy errors
rules.finding: The Volume Shadow Copy Service reported errors. Backups and restore points may be affected.
recommendations: Check the VSS writers (vssadmin list writers) and free space on the volume.

rules.title: Installation failures
rules.finding: A Windows Installer package failed to install.
recommendations: Check the product named in the event and free disk space; run the installer again as administrator.
